items.value: Only statement 3 is correct: the Committee examines members' credentials and reports to the General Assembly
items.reasoning: The Credentials Committee is a nine-member committee appointed by the General Assembly at the start of each session on the proposal of its President; it is not a Security Council body and does not work under Security Council supervision, so statement 1 fails and options B and D fall with it. Its function is exactly statement 3, to examine the credentials of the representatives of member States and report to the Assembly, which then approves the report. The claimed fixed calendar of March, June and September in statement 2 is not a feature of this committee, which meets during the Assembly session.

items.value: The Polar Code is the international code of safety for ships operating in polar waters
items.reasoning: The Polar Code is the International Maritime Organization's International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters, mandatory under SOLAS and MARPOL, covering ship design, construction, equipment, crew training and environmental protection in Arctic and Antarctic waters. It is a shipping safety and pollution instrument, not a territorial demarcation, a research protocol, or an Arctic Council trade and security pact.

items.value: All three statements about observer status in the UN General Assembly are correct
items.reasoning: The General Assembly grants observer status by resolution, and non-member States such as the Holy See and Palestine hold it, which is statement 1. Inter-governmental organisations, for instance the European Union and the African Union, may and do seek and receive observer status, which is statement 2. Permanent Observers are entitled to maintain permanent observer missions at United Nations Headquarters in New York, which is statement 3.

items.value: Only statements 1 and 4 are correct: the Tea Board is statutory and has overseas offices at Dubai and Moscow
items.reasoning: The Tea Board is a statutory body set up under the Tea Act, 1953, so statement 1 holds, and it maintains overseas promotion offices at Dubai and Moscow, so statement 4 holds. Statement 2 is wrong because the Board functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, and statement 3 is wrong because its head office is in Kolkata, not Bengaluru. Those two errors independently eliminate options A, B and C.

items.value: Greenwashing is conveying a false impression that a company's products are eco-friendly
items.reasoning: Greenwashing is a marketing and disclosure practice in which a firm projects an unwarranted image of environmental responsibility, through misleading labels, selective claims or unverifiable pledges, so that its products or operations appear greener than they are. The other options describe environmental accounting gaps, plain ecological negligence in project execution, and mandatory environmental provisioning, none of which involves the deceptive claim that defines the term.

items.value: Neither statement is correct; the warming and cooling roles of high and low clouds are the other way round
items.reasoning: High clouds such as cirrus are optically thin, so they let most incoming sunlight through while trapping outgoing longwave radiation and re-emitting it at very cold temperatures; their net effect is warming, not the cooling claimed in statement 1. Low clouds such as stratus and stratocumulus are optically thick with high albedo, so their reflection of solar radiation dominates and their net effect is cooling, not the warming claimed in statement 2; they do emit strongly in the infrared, but at nearly the surface temperature, so they trap little extra heat. Both statements therefore invert the standard cloud radiative forcing result.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct; Bidi Bidi is in Uganda, not Kenya
items.reasoning: Bidi Bidi is one of the world's largest refugee settlements but it lies in north-western Uganda, in Yumbe district near the South Sudan border, so statement 1 misplaces it in Kenya. It does house very large numbers of people who fled the South Sudanese civil war, which is statement 2, and the Dadaab complex in eastern Kenya has for decades sheltered refugees from the Somali civil war, which is statement 3.

items.value: Only Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan are members of the Organization of Turkic States
items.reasoning: The Organization of Turkic States, formerly the Turkic Council, comprises Turkey, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, with Hungary and Turkmenistan as observers. Of the countries listed, only Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan qualify. Armenia is not Turkic and is in fact adversarial to the grouping's core members, while Croatia and Romania are European states with no Turkic linkage.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: Kerala has the fully solar powered Cochin International Airport
items.reasoning: Cochin International Airport in Kerala became the world's first fully solar-powered airport, which makes statement 2 correct. Statement 1 fails because the largest solar park in India is Bhadla in Rajasthan, of roughly 2,245 MW, far larger than Gujarat's Charanka park. Statement 3 fails because the largest floating solar photovoltaic project in India is at Ramagundam in Telangana, with other big floating installations in Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, none in Goa.

items.value: All three statements correctly state UNCLOS provisions
items.reasoning: Article 3 of UNCLOS allows a coastal State to fix the breadth of its territorial sea up to 12 nautical miles from baselines drawn under the Convention, which is statement 1. Article 17 gives ships of all States, coastal and land-locked alike, the right of innocent passage through the territorial sea, which is statement 2. Article 57 caps the Exclusive Economic Zone at 200 nautical miles from the same baselines, which is statement 3.

items.value: China and Japan dispute the Senkaku Islands in the East China Sea
items.reasoning: The Senkaku Islands, called Diaoyu by China and Tiaoyutai by Taiwan, are uninhabited islands in the East China Sea administered by Japan and claimed by both China and Taiwan, and recurring incursions by Chinese coast guard vessels keep them in the news. They are natural, not artificial, islands and lie outside the South China Sea; there is no American base on them and no International Court of Justice ruling declaring them no man's land.

items.value: Three pairs are correct: Guinea, Lebanon and Tunisia; the Chad pairing is wrong
items.reasoning: Guinea saw its constitution and government suspended after the September 2021 military coup, Lebanon was in one of the most severe and prolonged economic depressions recorded anywhere in modern times, and Tunisia's President froze and then dissolved Parliament from July 2021, so pairs 2, 3 and 4 hold. Chad was in the news for the death of President Idriss Deby and the takeover by a military council, not for a Chinese permanent military base; China's only overseas base is in Djibouti, with reported plans elsewhere on the Atlantic coast, not Chad.

items.value: Only two pairs are correct: Anatolia with Turkey and Amhara with Ethiopia
items.reasoning: Anatolia is the Asian landmass of Turkey and Amhara is the Ethiopian region adjoining Tigray that featured heavily in the civil conflict, so pairs 1 and 2 hold. Cabo Delgado is the northern province of Mozambique hit by an Islamist insurgency, not a region of Spain, and Catalonia is the Spanish autonomous community around Barcelona, not part of Italy, so pairs 3 and 4 both fail.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: a protected animal is protected equally inside and outside protected areas
items.reasoning: Protection under the Wild Life (Protection) Act attaches to the species by virtue of its Schedule listing and operates throughout the territory, so a scheduled animal enjoys the same protection whether it is inside a national park or outside one, which is statement 2. Statement 1 overstates the law: Section 39 vests specified categories of wild animals, such as those hunted under permit or found dead, in the State Government, but the Act does not declare all wild animals the sole property of the government and it recognises certificates of ownership. Statement 3 is wrong because the Chief Wildlife Warden may permit capture or killing only where the animal has actually become dangerous to human life or is beyond recovery, and killing is a last resort after capture or tranquillisation is ruled out; mere apprehension is not enough.

items.value: Ants, notably the leafcutter and other attine species, cultivate fungi
items.reasoning: Fungus-growing ants of the tribe Attini, of which the leafcutter ants are the best known, cut and carry plant material into their nests as a substrate on which they deliberately grow a fungal crop that is their food, tending, weeding and even manuring the fungus garden. This is one of the classic examples of agriculture outside human societies. Cockroaches, crabs and spiders show no comparable cultivation behaviour.

items.value: Only two pairs are correct: Dhauli in Odisha and Erragudi in Andhra Pradesh
items.reasoning: Dhauli near Bhubaneswar in Odisha and Erragudi in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh are both major rock edict sites correctly located, so pairs 1 and 2 hold. Jaugada is also in Odisha, in Ganjam district, not Madhya Pradesh, and Kalsi lies in Dehradun district of Uttarakhand, not Karnataka, so pairs 3 and 4 fail.

items.value: Only two pairs are correct: Nannuka with the Chandelas and Nagabhata II with the Gurjara-Pratiharas
items.reasoning: Nannuka founded the Chandela line of Jejakabhukti and Nagabhata II was the Gurjara-Pratihara ruler who took Kanauj, so pairs 1 and 3 hold. Jayashakti, the Jeja after whom Jejakabhukti is named, was himself a Chandela and not a Paramara, and Bhoja is the celebrated Paramara king of Dhara, while Mihira Bhoja was a Gurjara-Pratihara; neither belongs to the Rashtrakutas. Pairs 2 and 4 therefore fail.

items.value: The social classification of Varna was known to the Sangam poets
items.reasoning: Sangam works, including the Tolkappiyam, are aware of the fourfold varna scheme and refer to brahmanas and other ranked groups alongside the indigenous tinai and kudi divisions, so option B stands. The other three are contradicted by the corpus itself: the poems are unusually rich in material detail about crops, trade goods and towns; the puram poems are built around a heroic warrior ethic of cattle raids, battle and hero-stones; and magical and supernatural forces are treated as real rather than dismissed as irrational.

items.value: During the reign of Akbar
items.reasoning: Nizamuddin Panipati rendered the Yogavasistha into Persian in the late 1590s for Prince Salim, the future Jahangir, while Akbar was on the throne. It belongs with the broader Mughal translation programme of Akbar's reign, which also produced Persian versions of the Mahabharata as the Razmnama, the Ramayana and the Atharva Veda.

items.value: Ramanuja taught that the best means of salvation was devotion
items.reasoning: Ramanuja propounded Vishishtadvaita, qualified monism, and held that intense loving devotion to Vishnu, culminating in surrender, was the surest path to salvation, a doctrine he opened to devotees regardless of birth. He accepted Vedic authority but that was not the distinctive core of his teaching; nor did he make dialectical reasoning or solitary meditation the primary means, which is what options C and D assert.

items.value: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Pran Pratishtha was performed by Rajendra Prasad, not Radhakrishnan
items.reasoning: Somnath is counted among the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva, which is statement 1, and Al-Biruni left a description of the temple in his account of India written in the early eleventh century, which is statement 2. Statement 3 is wrong on the person: the installation ceremony of the rebuilt temple in 1951 was performed by Dr Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, against Nehru's reservations, and not by S. Radhakrishnan, who became President only in 1962.

items.value: B cells and T cells protect the body from diseases caused by pathogens
items.reasoning: B lymphocytes and T lymphocytes are the effectors of adaptive immunity: B cells produce antibodies that neutralise and mark pathogens, while T cells kill infected cells and orchestrate the wider immune response. Their defining role is defence against pathogens. Allergen responses involve a misdirected immune reaction rather than being their purpose, they are not analgesic or anti-inflammatory agents, and they mount rather than suppress immune responses.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct; nanoparticles also occur naturally
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is false, since nanoparticles occur abundantly in nature in volcanic ash, sea spray, forest fire smoke, mineral weathering products and biological structures, quite apart from engineered ones. Statement 2 is true: metallic oxide nanoparticles such as titanium dioxide and zinc oxide are used in sunscreens and other cosmetics. Statement 3 is true as a matter of accepted concern, since some nanoparticles released from commercial products into air, water and soil can be toxic on inhalation or ingestion.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct; DNA barcoding cannot establish age
items.reasoning: DNA barcoding reads a short standardised gene region to assign a specimen to a species, so it is well suited to separating cryptic or morphologically similar species, which is statement 2, and to detecting undeclared or substituted plant and animal material in processed foods, which is statement 3. It cannot assess the age of an individual organism, since the barcode sequence is a species marker and does not change with the age of the specimen, so statement 1 fails.

items.value: Only nitrogen oxide and sulphur dioxide cause acid rain
items.reasoning: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen are oxidised and dissolved in atmospheric moisture to give sulphuric and nitric acids, so statements 2 and 4 apply. Carbon monoxide is a toxic product of incomplete combustion but does not form a strong acid in the atmosphere, and ozone is a secondary pollutant and oxidant, a component of photochemical smog rather than an acid-forming species in its own right.
